faq.question: What is the RabbitQA Accessibility module?
faq.answer: It is a web accessibility testing module that audits applications against WCAG 2.2 and European Accessibility Act requirements. It combines Lighthouse-backed automated audits, versioned score tracking, and AI fix recommendations with screen reader testing delivered with the engagement.

faq.question: Which standards does it cover?
faq.answer: Testing is aligned to WCAG 2.2 and the European Accessibility Act (EAA). Each audit also records performance, best-practices, and SEO scores alongside accessibility, with per-check counts of passed, failed, manual, and not-applicable results.

faq.question: How is screen reader testing delivered?
faq.answer: Screen reader coverage across JAWS, NVDA and VoiceOver comes with the engagement, run by our QA team and reported back into the same project as the automated findings, so manual assistive-technology results and automated audit results live side by side.

faq.question: Can it audit pages behind a login?
faq.answer: Yes. Configure basic form authentication login URL, field selectors, credentials, and wait time or use the advanced script mode, which passes through a security sanitizer before execution, to audit authenticated areas of your application.

faq.question: What happens after an issue is found?
faq.answer: Each failed check can generate an AI recommendation describing the problem, a suggested fix, and a verification step. Your team reviews and applies the fix, then re-runs the audit, and the new result is stored as another versioned run, so the score trend shows the improvement.

faq.question: How do I track progress over time?
faq.answer: Every analysis is saved as a versioned run with its scores and check counts. Suites average their audits and projects keep an overall score, while dashboards surface top-performing projects, projects needing attention, and recent activity.

faq.question: What is BrowserHub?
faq.answer: BrowserHub is RabbitQA's cloud browser testing module. It provides a managed browser inventory with capability-based provisioning for live, interactive sessions and automated runs plus HAR network recording, files, reports, and settings all scoped to your RabbitQA project and built on the same cloud as MobileHub's device fleet.

faq.question: How is BrowserHub different from MobileHub?
faq.answer: MobileHub provides mobile device testing on real devices and emulators; BrowserHub provides browser testing on the same cloud. They share session, file, report, and API-key foundations, so evidence from both lands in the same RabbitQA project.

faq.question: Can I run automated browser tests?
faq.answer: Yes. BrowserHub provisions automated sessions over standard WebDriver on Selenium Grid-based infrastructure. Sessions are created, polled, and terminated through the platform, and automation clients authenticate with scoped API keys.

faq.question: Does BrowserHub capture network traffic?
faq.answer: Yes. Sessions support HAR network recording, so you can inspect the requests, responses, and third-party calls behind a failure instead of reconstructing them.

faq.question: Which browsers and versions are available?
faq.answer: The inventory is managed through capability-based provisioning with version-retention policies; contact us for the current matrix.

faq.question: What is MobileHub?
faq.answer: MobileHub is RabbitQA's mobile device testing module. It provides browser-based access to a shared fleet of real Android and iOS devices and emulators for live manual testing and Appium automation, with reservations, evidence capture, issue tracking, and usage reporting scoped to your project.

faq.question: Does MobileHub include real devices or emulators?
faq.answer: Both. The shared fleet combines real Android and iOS hardware with emulators and simulators across multiple OS versions. You can filter by real or emulator type before starting a session, and the dashboard's fleet breakdown shows the mix at a glance.

faq.question: How does automation work in MobileHub?
faq.answer: MobileHub supports Appium-based automation UiAutomator2 for Android and XCUITest for iOS. A built-in Config Generator produces capabilities and code samples in Java, Python, Node.js, and cURL. Automation clients authenticate with scoped API keys or the MobileHub CLI, and submitted runs group into builds and sessions.

faq.question: Can I test location-based scenarios?
faq.answer: Yes. Location Simulation sets the device's GPS position from a map click, exact coordinates, or preset cities such as London, Berlin, and New York. The simulated location clears automatically when the session ends, so devices return to a clean state.

faq.question: How do bugs get tracked?
faq.answer: You can raise an issue directly from a session screenshot or link the session to an existing issue. Issues associate with TestPilot plans and test runs, carry their evidence as attachments, and are managed on RabbitQA's native board or on Jira and Azure DevOps boards when those integrations are configured.

faq.question: Can I reserve a device for later?
faq.answer: Yes. Reserve any available device for a specific date, time slot, and duration from 15 minutes to 4 hours, with a stated purpose. Reservations can be edited or cancelled, and history is retained.

faq.question: Does MobileHub test websites too?
faq.answer: MobileHub focuses on mobile devices. Browser testing is handled by BrowserHub, its sibling module on the same device cloud, which provides browser inventory, live and automated browser sessions, and HAR network recording.
